feedback: On the gas challenge: explain that air and CO2 have mass and the carbon in CO2 becomes part of the plant's solid body over time.
On the plant-food challenge: fertiliser supplies small amounts of minerals for health, not the bulk material; the bulk comes from CO2 and water. Distinguish minerals from mass.
Credit arguments that cite the barely-changed soil as evidence, not just assertions of the correct answer.
activities.intendedInsight: Defending the claim aloud - not just recognising the right answer - rehearses the argue-from-evidence practice and can surface any residual 'soil' or 'water-only' thinking.
learnerActions: Face a skeptical partner (or role-play one) who insists 'the tree's wood obviously came from the soil it grew in - convince me otherwise.'
Marshal the mass-balance evidence out loud: state the figures (plant +kg, soil -grams) and reason that the soil could not be the source.
Respond to follow-up challenges: 'Carbon dioxide is a gas - how can a gas become solid wood?' and 'A gardener adds plant food to the pot - isn't that where the mass comes from?'
Keep arguing until the skeptic concedes only to sound reasoning.
activities.title: Defend the claim against a skeptic

feedback: Watch the common slip: conceding 'water comes from soil' and then wrongly extending it to 'so all the mass comes from soil'. Water is from soil, but the carbon-carrying material is from the air.
If you labelled minerals as the plant's 'food', revise: minerals are small quantities for health; the bulk material is carbon, oxygen and hydrogen from CO2 and water.
activities.intendedInsight: Water coming from the soil does not mean all the mass comes from the soil; minerals are a tiny health contribution, and the bulk material is CO2 + water. This sets up photosynthesis without overreaching the mechanism.
learnerActions: Draw an arrow model: CO2 (from air) + water (from soil) -> plant material, with soil minerals shown as a thin side-arrow.
Explain in a sentence the different jobs: water comes from the soil (and is a source of material); air supplies carbon dioxide; soil minerals come in small amounts for health, not bulk.
State the forward link lightly: the invisible air gas plus water become the plant's food and structure (this is photosynthesis), without writing any chemical equation.
activities.title: Separate the minerals from the mass; bridge to photosynthesis
